This test flight marked the 13th attempt for the Starship program. The recent flight was the second for the V3 version of Starship. This was also the first flight conducted by SpaceX as a publicly traded company.

stories.title: Deep breathing: the asthma clinic buried 250 metres into an Armenian salt mine
stories.summary: An underground asthma clinic in Armenia is located 250 meters deep in a salt mine and has been operational since 1987. Patients undergo speleotherapy, which is believed to alleviate respiratory diseases through salt-saturated air. The clinic's future is uncertain after the Armenian government withdrew state funding. Activities such as billiards and breathing exercises are encouraged to aid patients during their treatment.

stories.title: First person gets new experimental vaccine for Ebola
stories.summary: The first volunteer in the world, a 37-year-old UK man called Ed Hunt, has received an experimental vaccine against the Ebola virus. The vaccine, designed using the same technology as one of the UK's Covid vaccines, was given in Oxford where scientists developed it in just eight weeks. Hunt is the first of 50 healthy volunteers aged 18-55 being recruited for the trial. The vaccine uses the same technology as the Oxford AstraZeneca Covid jab which was given to hundreds of millions of people during the pandemic.

stories.title: 'Life-changing' MS drug to help people walk now on NHS in England
stories.summary: The first drug to help people with multiple sclerosis walk, called fampridine, is now available on the NHS in England. Fampridine boosts nerve signals to make it easier for some people to move and live independently. Clinical trials showed that around four in 10 people taking the drug had improvements in their walking speed and endurance. The drug has previously been rejected for use by the NHS in England due to cost concerns, but it is already available elsewhere in the UK.

stories.title: UK humanitarian worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital
stories.summary: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) reported that a UK resident is being monitored for Ebola at a London hospital. The individual has no symptoms and is being assessed as a precautionary measure after working with a humanitarian organization in response to the Ebola outbreak. The incubation period for Ebola ranges from two to 21 days, during which the individual must isolate. There are currently no confirmed cases of Ebola in the UK.

stories.title: UK begins trials of Ebola vaccine developed in just eight weeks
stories.summary: A new Ebola vaccine developed in just eight weeks by scientists at the University of Oxford has entered clinical trials. The vaccine targets the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which has caused an ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with 625 deaths and 1,792 confirmed cases. The trial will involve 50 healthy adults aged 18-55 in the UK, with researchers also preparing for trials in Africa. The vaccine uses the same technology as the Oxford/AstraZeneca Covid vaccine, employing a genetically modified chimpanzee cold virus to deliver a snippet of Ebola genetic code.

stories.title: Organic eggs have worse impact on climate than eggs from caged chickens
stories.summary: Research indicates that organic eggs have a greater negative impact on the climate than eggs from caged chickens. Transitioning to an organic free-range model in the UK could result in greenhouse gas emissions equivalent to 2,316,000 tonnes of CO2. The study highlighted that organic free-range production requires more chickens for the same egg output, making it less efficient. The research also pointed out that organic farming has higher mortality rates among chickens.

stories.title: Kenya investigating unexpected deaths of 15 elephants in national park
stories.summary: Kenya is investigating the unexplained deaths of 15 elephants in Amboseli National Park. The Kenya Wildlife Service reported that 10 of the elephants showed signs of partial paralysis before dying. Preliminary tests detected a potential toxic substance in some of the elephants, while other tests were negative for toxins. Environmental investigations are being conducted to determine if there was a common source of exposure.

stories.title: Ghana mourns its tallest man - a 'generous and popular giant'
stories.summary: Sulemana Abdul Samed, Ghana's tallest man, passed away at the age of 33 in a hospital in Tamale. He was known for his generosity and had become a local celebrity due to his height of 7ft 4in. His death has left the community of Gambaga in shock and mourning.
